correctness.rationale: With X=uφ and Y=sψ and φ(u)=ψ(s)=0, write a=φ(s) and b=ψ(u). The opposite products are a uψ and b sφ. This yields the necessary trace and annihilation conditions, including in characteristic two. For both nonzero, write the fixed products P=uρ, Q=sσ with common trace λ; all solutions are X=u(aσ/λ), Y=s(ρ/a) for a≠0. The reciprocal scalar action is free and transitive. In the one-sided case the image line of Y lies in ker ρ but differs from ku, and each of its L_(n−1)−1 possibilities allows (q−1)q^(n−2) covectors for X; this vanishes at n=2. For (0,0), the line of Y lies in ker φ and its covector annihilates both image lines; coincident and distinct lines give q^(n−1)−1 and q^(n−2)−1 choices respectively. This proves Z and K. For a fixed nonzero-trace P, eligible Q have L_(n−1)q^(n−2) possibilities, giving H and the mass identity. In odd characteristic the linear change to (J,C) is invertible. The q−1 count in the Jordan–Lie prose is scoped to rank two; there are q(q+1) ordered image-plane decompositions for fixed admissible J and two sign choices of J for fixed admissible C. The supplied verification evidence is exhaustive only for its listed prime-field dimensions; the proof instead treats arbitrary prime powers. The uploaded checker was not executed.
